text.p: Germany's Ford-Werke AG said on Tuesday that it had agreed an investment pact with employees which would secure its five plants in Germany and would save the group $120 million a year.
Ford-Werke management said the investment pact with the works representative council guaranteed production at its plants in Cologne, Saarlouis, Dueren, Wuelfrath and Berlin.
The Ford-Werke group will in return make savings worth around $120 million which will come from cuts to additional bonus payments and the introduction of flexible working time.
Ford said wages would not be cut. Ford-Werke management board chairman William Boddie described the agreement as a "milestone in the history of Ford-Werke AG".
Boddie said the agreement showed it was possible to come to agreement if one was flexible on pay awards.
Ford has a payroll of around 34,000 employees in Germany. The new measures will be implemented in harmony with existing pay awards on shift work and flexible working time.

Management said the agreement ensured that the building of a three-cylinder engine in Cologne, with start-up capacity of 20,000 units, would continue as planned, as well as the development of the next generation of its Mondeo model.
The agreement would also guarantee the production of the successor to the Escort model at Ford's Saarlouis plant.
